title: Rational nodes and normalization branches of nodal fibres
statement:
Let $f:X	o S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Its quasi-split nodal-fibre condition is the following predicate. For every $t\in S$, form the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ over $\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-weil-residue-field]. For every point $x\in X_t$ at which $X_t	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the canonical residue-field map $\kappa(t)	o\kappa(x)$ is surjective, there are exactly two points above $x$ under the componentwise reduced normalization $
u:X_t^
u	o X_t$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and for every such point $z$ the canonical map $\kappa(t)	o\kappa(z)$ induced by $X_t^
u	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is surjective. Thus, for a nodal family, every singular point and both of its branches are rational over the base residue field. Smoothness of the irreducible components is not required.

source.place: Definition of quasi-split semi-stable curves immediately before Lemma 5.7, pp.614--615. Read the public primary scan https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.1575.pdf (PDF pages 16--17).
